quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #6
										  					
  

50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: At a stop sign, you should stop and:

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for tailgating cars.
Move when the vehicle ahead of you moves.
Look right, then left, then right again.
Look left, then right, then left again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look left, then right, then left again.
questions.explanation: Look left first because vehicles from the left are closer to you. Then look right, then left again in case you missed a vehicle the first time.

questions.question: Which drugs can affect your driving ability?

options.text: Allergy medicine
Marijuana
Cold remedies
All of these choices

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these choices
questions.explanation: Many drugs can affect your driving. This includes illegal drugs and legal medicines you buy with or without a prescription. Driving while impaired by any drug is illegal.

questions.question: A good rule for passing is:

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
Get to the front of slow traffic so you can see better.
Always flash your lights and honk to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
questions.explanation: Each pass increases the risk of a crash. If you drive faster than others, you will need to keep passing. Drive with traffic flow at the legal speed limit and pass only when necessary.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: It is okay to follow motorcycles closely.
A motorcycle with two riders is more balanced than one with one rider.
When passing a motorcycle, change lanes completely.
A motorcycle's brake lights turn on when the rider slows down.

questions.correctAnswerText: When passing a motorcycle, change lanes completely.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles need a full lane width. Move your vehicle completely into the left lane before passing a motorcycle.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: Railroad crossing.
One-way traffic.
Limited parking.
Playground ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossing.
questions.explanation: Round signs show railroad crossings. This sign warns you that a railroad crossing is coming. Look for trains.

questions.question: Your brake lights tell other drivers that you:

options.text: Are making a turn.
Have your emergency brake on.
Are changing lanes.
Are slowing down or stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Are slowing down or stopping.
questions.explanation: Brake lights show other drivers that you are slowing down or stopping. Always keep your brake lights working.

questions.question: A steady yellow light means:

options.text: Go.
Yield to other cars.
Slow down and prepare to stop.
Stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and prepare to stop.
questions.explanation: A yellow light means a red light is coming soon. Slow down and be ready to stop. If you are already in the intersection or cannot stop safely, continue through with care.

questions.question: The driver's left arm points downward. This hand signal means:

options.text: Turn left.
Turn right.
Stop.
Start up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: Left arm pointing down means the driver will stop. Adjust your driving if you are following this vehicle.

questions.question: This sign prevents:

options.text: Entering full parking lots.
Entering road construction areas.
Entering dead-end streets.
Entering one-way streets and expressway ramps from the wrong direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Entering one-way streets and expressway ramps from the wrong direction.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that traffic flows one way. You cannot enter from your current direction.

questions.question: When approaching a railroad crossing without traffic signals, you should:

options.text: Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be prepared to stop.
All railroad crossings have signals, so this will not happen.
Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be prepared to stop.
questions.explanation: At unmarked railroad crossings, slow down and be ready to stop. Look both ways on all tracks for trains. If you see or hear a train, stop at a safe distance and wait until it passes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turns.
Right turns are allowed.
Stop before turning right.
Sharp curve ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turns.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red slash through it means you cannot do that action. You cannot turn right where this sign is posted.

questions.question: Which statement about emergency vehicles is true?

options.text: They have the right-of-way when using sirens, horns, and flashing lights.
They can use loudspeakers to give instructions.
They can follow each other.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: You must let emergency vehicles (police, fire trucks, ambulances) go first when they use sirens or flashing lights. Follow any instructions they give over loudspeakers. Multiple emergency vehicles often travel together, so wait until the road is completely clear before moving.

questions.question: What should you do when you see an emergency vehicle with flashing lights?

options.text: Slow down and stay in your lane.
Keep driving in your lane.
Pull to the right and stop.
Stop right where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights or hear a siren from an emergency vehicle, pull over to the right side of the road immediately and stop.

questions.question: When turning left onto a one-way street, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The right lane.
The lane closest to where you came from.
Either lane.
Neither lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to where you came from.
questions.explanation: Always turn into the lane that is closest to the lane you are leaving.

questions.question: When making a turn, you must ____ your speed.

options.text: Increase
Keep the same
Change
Slow down

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down
questions.explanation: Slow down before turning so you can control your vehicle, stay in your lane, and handle unexpected situations.

questions.question: What does a green arrow on a lane control signal mean?

options.text: You may use this lane.
No traffic is allowed in this lane.
You have the right-of-way.
You must move into this lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may use this lane.
questions.explanation: A green arrow pointing down means you can use that lane.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Watch for bicycles.
Bicycles are not allowed.
Bicycle repair shop ahead.
Bicycles have the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for bicycles.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that bicycles may be in the area ahead.

questions.question: How can you help prevent rear-end collisions?

options.text: Avoid sudden stops.
Check your mirrors and blind spots before stopping.
Release the gas pedal before applying the brakes.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Sudden stops make it hard for drivers behind you to avoid hitting you. Release the gas to let your car slow first, then apply steady brake pressure. This gives drivers behind you time to react.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Bicycle crossing.
Stop only if other cars are approaching.
Bicycle store.
Soft shoulders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Bicycle crossing.
questions.explanation: This sign shows where bicycles cross or ride next to the road. Drive carefully in this area because bicycles are likely present.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow line on your side of the centerline mean?

options.text: Slow down.
Pass with caution.
Do not pass.
Keep right on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass other vehicles.

questions.question: You are in an accident. What should you do?

options.text: Stop immediately.
Help the injured.
Call the police.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Stop your vehicle right away. If you can, move it out of traffic. Call the police and ask for an ambulance if needed. Do not move injured people unless necessary. Apply direct pressure to stop heavy bleeding. Wait for emergency help.

questions.question: How can you help prevent crashes?

options.text: Communicate with other road users.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Communicate with other road users.
questions.explanation: Many crashes happen because one driver surprises others. Communicate with drivers, cyclists, and pedestrians by using signals when you slow down, stop, or turn. Use your emergency lights or horn when needed.

questions.question: Distracted driving is:

options.text: Very uncommon.
Extremely risky behavior.
Nothing to be concerned about.
No less safe than driving under any other conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Extremely risky behavior.
questions.explanation: Distracted driving is very dangerous. It puts you, your passengers, pedestrians, cyclists, and other drivers at risk. Staying focused on driving helps prevent crashes.

questions.question: Which of these does not happen after drinking alcohol?

options.text: Your reflexes and reaction time slow down.
Your judgement of speed and distance is distorted.
You are less alert.
You calm down and can concentrate better.

questions.correctAnswerText: You calm down and can concentrate better.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your reaction time, reduces your ability to see clearly, changes how you judge speed and distance, reduces your ability to recover from headlight glare, and makes you more likely to take risks.

questions.question: What affects your ability to stop?

options.text: Signal lights.
Other cars on the road.
The time of day.
The condition of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The condition of the road.
questions.explanation: Road condition greatly affects your ability to stop. Slow down when roads are poor so you can stay in control. Driving too fast on slippery roads puts you at risk if you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: What is a speed limit?

options.text: The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel on a road under dangerous conditions.
The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel on a road under ideal conditions.
The suggested speed to travel on a road under ideal conditions.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The maximum or minimum legal speed you can travel on a road under ideal conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the maximum or minimum legal speed for ideal conditions. You can drive slower than the posted limit, but you cannot drive faster. Drive slower in school zones, work zones, or when conditions like bad weather or construction make the posted speed unsafe.

questions.question: What does this black and yellow sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is for one-way traffic only.
Due to roadwork, there is a detour to the right.
Slow down because the road ahead curves sharply.
There is a crossroad to your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down because the road ahead curves sharply.
questions.explanation: This sign shows that the road ahead curves sharply in one direction. Slow down before you reach this sharp curve, just as you would at a sharp turn at an intersection.

questions.question: When you encounter an aggressive driver, you should:

options.text: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
Cut them off to slow them down.
Retaliate by tailgating them.
Make sure they know you disapprove of their behavior.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid eye contact, slow down, and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If another driver is threatening you or driving dangerously, stay calm. Slow down and let them pass. Put distance between your vehicles. Do not make eye contact or make rude gestures.

questions.question: You see a flashing red light at an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe to do so.
Stop only if other cars are also approaching the intersection.
Stop only if other cars are already within the intersection.
Slow down and be prepared to stop, if necessary.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a full stop and go when it is safe to do so.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must stop completely, yield the right-of-way, and proceed only when it is safe.

questions.question: You miss your exit on the interstate. What should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Make a U-turn to go back to the exit.
Continue driving and use the next exit.
Put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue driving and use the next exit.
questions.explanation: Do not make a sudden turn into an exit you almost missed. Continue to the next exit.

questions.question: You reach an intersection where you want to turn, but you are not in the right lane. What should you do?

options.text: Quickly cut across traffic to make your turn.
Turn on your blinker and turn from your current lane.
Go to the next intersection and turn there.
Safely change lanes then put your vehicle in reverse to go back to the intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go to the next intersection and turn there.
questions.explanation: Do not make last-minute turns. If you are not in the right lane to turn, drive to the next intersection. Then make your turn from the correct lane.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalks, where should a pedestrian walk?

options.text: On the side with the lightest traffic.
On the same side where traffic is moving.
On the side facing oncoming traffic.
On the side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Pedestrians should walk on the side of the road facing traffic. This way they can see vehicles coming toward them.

questions.question: You are borrowing an unfamiliar car from a friend. What should you do?

options.text: Do not worry because all vehicles are the same.
Hide that you are unfamiliar with the car.
Ignore any obvious problems to avoid embarrassing your friend.
Take a few minutes to learn where all the controls are and how they work.

questions.correctAnswerText: Take a few minutes to learn where all the controls are and how they work.
questions.explanation: Before driving an unfamiliar car, spend a few minutes learning the location and operation of the turn signals, hazard lights, headlights, windshield wipers, brakes, gear selector, and horn. Fix any problems before driving.

questions.question: What does a flashing yellow light mean?

options.text: Stop and look for other vehicles. Go if there is no traffic.
Stop and wait for a green light.
Speed up to clear the intersection quickly.
Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed with caution.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution. Keep alert for other traffic.

questions.question: ____ limit your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory.

options.text: Only a blood alcohol level greater than the legal limit can
Alcohol does not
Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
Only a blood alcohol level greater than 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even the smallest amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Even a small amount of alcohol reduces your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Your driving skills will suffer. No one can drink and drive safely.

questions.question: What does a yellow and black diamond-shaped sign mean?

options.text: It warns you about conditions on or near the road.
It helps you find cities and towns ahead.
It tells you about traffic laws and regulations.
It tells you about road construction ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: It warns you about conditions on or near the road.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black symbols or words on a yellow background. They warn you about conditions ahead on or near the road.

questions.question: When passing a vehicle on a two-lane road, what should you do?

options.text: Return to the right lane when there is enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.
Stay in the left lane if you plan to turn left.
Return to the right side of the road immediately.
Drive in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Return to the right lane when there is enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.
questions.explanation: When passing on a two-lane road, return to the right lane once you have enough space between you and the vehicle you passed.

questions.question: When can you use flashing hazard lights?

options.text: When your vehicle is stopped or broken down on the highway or shoulder.
When rain reduces visibility.
When driving at night.
In heavy traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: When your vehicle is stopped or broken down on the highway or shoulder.
questions.explanation: Use flashing hazard lights only when your vehicle is disabled or legally stopped on the highway or shoulder. You may also use them in a funeral procession.

questions.question: You are in an accident and another person is injured. What should you do?

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene immediately.
Always leave the injured person where they are.
Do not move the injured unnecessarily. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move the injured unnecessarily. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move injured people unless necessary. Improper handling can make injuries worse. Keep them warm until help arrives. If there is heavy bleeding, apply direct pressure to stop it.

questions.question: Roads freeze quickly when they are:

options.text: Flat.
Curvy.
In the sun.
Shaded.

questions.correctAnswerText: Shaded.
questions.explanation: In cold or wet weather, be careful on shaded areas under trees or buildings. These areas freeze faster than other parts of the road and are the last to dry.

questions.question: When can you NOT cross a single broken white or yellow line?

options.text: When it would interfere with other traffic.
When turning left into a driveway.
When the car in front of you is broken down.
When passing on the right on a one-way street.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it would interfere with other traffic.
questions.explanation: You can cross a single broken line to pass or change lanes. You can do this only if it is safe and does not interfere with other traffic.

questions.question: What is true about drivers who have consumed alcohol before driving?

options.text: They always know the risks they are taking.
They cannot control their bodies, minds, or vehicles properly.
They are better drivers because they are more careful.
They have faster reaction times.

questions.correctAnswerText: They cannot control their bodies, minds, or vehicles properly.
questions.explanation: Alcohol slows your thinking, vision, focus, and reaction time. It is never safe to drink any amount of alcohol before driving.

questions.question: What should you do when an emergency vehicle with flashing red or blue lights is approaching?

options.text: Try to reach your destination before the emergency vehicle catches up.
Keep driving but try to stay out of its way.
Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
Stop in the middle of an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the side of the road and stop completely.
questions.explanation: You must let all emergency vehicles pass. Pull to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then pull over.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
Side road.
Two-way left turn.
Farm machinery.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop.
questions.explanation: Eight-sided signs mean STOP. You must stop and let other traffic go if they have the right-of-way. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: What usually causes hydroplaning?

options.text: Stopping too many times.
Stopping suddenly.
Turning suddenly.
Driving too fast.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving too fast.
questions.explanation: When you drive too fast on wet roads, your tires cannot push water away. They lose grip and slide on the water. This is called hydroplaning.

questions.question: A load that extends more than ____ past the back of a vehicle must have a red flag during the day.

options.text: One foot
Two feet
Three feet
Four feet

questions.correctAnswerText: Four feet
questions.explanation: If a load sticks out more than four feet from the back of your vehicle, you must use a red flag (18 inches square) during the day. At night or in poor visibility, use red lights and reflectors instead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Low clearance.
Fines double in a work zone.
No left turn.
Do not block intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low clearance.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell you about hazards ahead. This sign warns that there is not much space above the road.

questions.question: What does a diamond-shaped sign do?

options.text: Warns of dangers or hazards ahead.
Alerts you to school zones.
Alerts you to parks and recreation areas.
Alerts you to food and gas stops.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warns of dangers or hazards ahead.
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs warn you about hazards. They are usually yellow or orange.

questions.question: If you drink alcohol socially, what is the best way to drive safely?

options.text: Drink coffee before driving.
Get a ride home with someone who has not been drinking.
Take a cold shower before driving.
Wait 30 minutes after drinking before driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get a ride home with someone who has not been drinking.
questions.explanation: The best way to stay safe is to have a sober friend drive you home. Coffee and cold showers do not reduce alcohol in your system. Your body needs about one hour to process one drink.

questions.question: What is the minimum amount of Personal Injury Protection (PIP) and Property Damage Liability (PDL) insurance you must have?
questions.explanation: Florida law requires all drivers to have at least $10,000 in PIP insurance and $10,000 in PDL insurance. You must show proof of this insurance when you register your vehicle.
